policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV reads 'His ways are firm at all times'. The qere is plural (Ncbpc) and the ketiv singular (Ncbsc); ASV renders grammatical number reliably, so the plural distinguishes the qere.

The ketiv carries a conjunction the qere lacks. ASV begins the clause 'He croucheth' without 'And', which points to the qere, but ASV freely drops a connective, so this does not distinguish the readings.

ASV reads 'And the helpless fall by his strong ones'. The qere is two words, 'host of the unfortunate', whose first word ASV does not render at all; the ketiv is the single word 2489 that 'the helpless' translates. The word count and the absent noun distinguish the ketiv.
The same near-synonymous pair as PSA.9.12; ASV reads 'the poor'. Left undetermined on the same reasoning.
